title: A fin de que + subjuntivo: el propósito de una acción conjunta

sections.content: A fin de que + subjunctive states the purpose behind an action when the subject of the purpose clause differs from the subject doing the acting -- the collective counterpart to con el fin de + infinitive, which only works when both subjects match. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Bolívar había soñado con una confederación unida, a fin de que las nuevas repúblicas no quedaran aisladas y débiles.
items.english: Bolívar had dreamed of a united confederation, so that the new republics wouldn't remain isolated and weak.

items.spanish: Varios países crearon la ALALC, a fin de que la industrialización pudiera beneficiarse de mercados más amplios.
items.english: Several countries created LAFTA, so that industrialization could benefit from broader markets.

items.spanish: Cada gobierno aplicaba proteccionismo, a fin de que sus industrias nacionales no sufrieran una competencia externa directa.
items.english: Each government applied protectionism, so that its national industries wouldn't suffer direct foreign competition.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos buscaron ampliar sus mercados, a fin de que sus economías superaran definitivamente la crisis de la deuda.
items.english: Governments sought to expand their markets, so that their economies would definitively overcome the debt crisis.

sections.content: Use a fin de que + subjunctive whenever the person or thing benefiting from the purpose is different from the one acting -- if they're the same, switch to a fin de + infinitive instead, just like para que vs. para.
